synth.vision: Make the product the validated, offline-first, tamper-evident QC LIMS for small and mid-size pharma labs, and make it bilingual (Arabic RTL and English). The closest comparison is LabWare, STARLIMS, SampleManager and LabVantage. Order of work: R1 closes the integrity holes, so no OOS or empty sample can be released, signatures always verify, MFA cannot be bypassed, and the data survives upgrade and restore. R2 adds the depth buyers expect from the incumbents: versioned specs and methods, calculation engine, controlled CoA, custody and storage, reagents, stability, EM, worklists, instrument capture, QMS and SOP/training control. R3 adds what the incumbents do not do well: Arabic/RTL with locale-safe GxP dates, SPC/OOT trending with shelf-life estimation, zero-install embedded PostgreSQL with least-privilege roles, directory sign-on, archival, and global search. Every change keeps the AGENTS.md rules: audit in the same transaction, e-signatures with meaning and recordVersion, optimistic concurrency, strict Zod, actor from req.user.

releases.name: R1 Foundation and integrity
releases.goal: Make the existing system trustworthy and upgradeable. Split api.ts and schema.ts into per-domain modules so later work runs in parallel. Close the critical integrity and security defects: OOS-blind release, MFA bypass, the spec-approval FK failure, failed-signature bookkeeping rolled back, fabricated data, and timestamp corruption in backup. Add the migration runner, scheduler and backup v2. Order: r1-core first (serial), then r1-migrations, r1-identity, r1-build-shell and r1-client-shell, then r1-esign, r1-audit, r1-authz, then the domain tracks. Migration numbers are reserved per track: 0000-0009 migrations, 0010 identity, 0020 esign, 0030 audit, 0040 authz, 0050 results-oos, 0060 spec, 0070 quality-fixes, 0080 backup-jobs. Rule for all later work: the samples and results core tables are frozen (their columns feed signed hashes). New sample or result features add 1:1 sidecar tables (sample_<feature>, result_<feature>) so tracks never edit the same schema file. Result guards, transition guards, release blockers, job handlers and schedules are directory registries, so each track adds its own file instead of editing a shared one.

tracks.summary: Runs alone first. Characterization test (route-table.json), then a mechanical move of every route into src/server/routes/<domain>.ts: auth, admin, training, eln, notebook-templates, samples, results, oos, release, specifications, instruments, reagents, env, stability, traceability, audit, signatures, dashboard, reports, ai, backup, jobs, system, lookup. Also split lims.ts into per-domain validation files and make server.ts a thin composer of http/security.ts, http/static.ts and realtime.ts. Domain route and validation files transfer to the owning tracks on merge. Adds core primitives and the Vitest harness. Express stays on 4 with the asyncHandler wrapper.

Repo hygiene and config: delete the 143 root scripts (tag the legacy commit), remove Firebase and xlsx, self-host fonts, add typed Zod config, add a strict server tsconfig with a baseline file. Shell and HTTP hardening: production-by-default, loopback bind, CSP, server bundle moved out of the static root, IPC sender checks, stable port, permission handler, per-user JSON rate limits, pino logs, /api/health and /api/ready, crash supervision. Seed script split into scripts/dev/seed/index.ts plus per-domain seeds/*.ts.

Versioned forward-only migrations in drizzle/ with a checksum runner, pre-migration verified backup, downgrade guard and SYSTEM_MIGRATION audit. Includes the timestamptz conversion, the counters table, the index set, and the append-only trigger registry (src/db/protections/<domain>.ts). Splits schema.ts into per-domain files handed to the owning tracks: identity, signatures, audit, samples, oos, specifications, eln, equipment, ops.

Purpose-typed tokens, working TOTP enrolment, replay and throttle protection, encrypted TOTP secrets, sessions table with idle and absolute timeout and logout, user create/reset/deactivate, password policy and history, split login and signing lockouts, login/lockout/logout security events, break-glass CLI, training-certify fix. Keystore and AI egress control: AI off by default, no canned output, labelled drafts.

apiFetch client with typed errors and 401 handling, session guard with idle lock and re-auth that keeps unsaved form state, ErrorBoundary, working MFA and forced password-change screens, and removal of the static 'Validated/Compliant' badges and of the atob token decode. Develops against the /auth/me and /auth/reauth contract from r1-identity.

One signRecord service, polymorphic signatures (entity_type, entity_id, nullable FK), signature_meanings catalog, name and role snapshot, failure bookkeeping committed in its own transaction, TOTP step-up, training exemption keyed to the meaning, and verification for every entity type. Other tracks migrate their own signing calls to it.

Audit v2: actor snapshot columns, hash_version/hash_alg, one shared chain verifier (duplicate route removed, Admin/QA only), checkpoints and bounded signature verification, keyset-paged and filtered /audit with CSV export, security_events chain, audit viewer and per-record History tab.

Permission tables with a default matrix migrated from the four roles. Central route-to-permission table applied as middleware (no edits to route files) with a boot-time deny-by-default assertion. Entity state-machine definitions, shared record-level SoD helper, role-change e-signature, exported matrix, and a fuzz test that posts unknown keys to every mutating route.

Server evaluator with USP 7.20 rounding, auto-opened OOS in the result transaction, result-entry role and state rules, completeness and OOS gates on review, approve and batch release, and OOS status vocabulary and legal transitions. Also the isOOS rename and Reports.tsx hotfixes, and the guard, result-guard and release-blocker registries. Sample id via per-year counter, cursor-paged GET /samples, set-based bulk import, spec binding.

Specification lifecycle: author, revision_label separate from the OCC counter, strict parameter schema with unit, limit kind and decimals, effective-date selection, SoD approval through signRecord (fixes the FK failure), and resolveActiveSpec() for registration.

ELN: author-only signing, server-chosen meaning, untruncated audit, template audit and role, notebook entries blocked after Approved. Hotfix wave: calibrate (role, date validation, history, signature), reagent receipt with a verified password, grade-aware EM limits, stability status and edit lock, honest dashboard, and batch-material defaults removed.

Backup v2 (streamed, text-exact timestamps, blob section, scheduled run, mirror copy, retention, restore drill) and the DB-backed job queue with node-cron registry and start-up catch-up. Hotfixes: job ownership check, and CoA PDF refused for non-Approved samples with a DRAFT watermark.

mergedGaps.title: Platform core: api.ts split, transactional primitives, central validation and errors, test harness [PLT-03+SEC-06+PLT-06 harness]

mergedGaps.title: Versioned migrations, schema split, timestamptz fix, indexes [G2+QA-04+PLT-02+PLT-09 indexes]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: Incumbents ship upgrade packages with pre-upgrade backup and scripted migration. Nobody re-initialises the database to take a patch.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: init-db.ts:20-26 applies schema.sql only when public.users is absent. There is no migrations folder and no schema version. CI uses drizzle-kit push while the installer ships schema.sql. Timestamps are timestamp without tz with defaultNow(), evaluated in the PG session zone but read by drizzle as UTC. There are no indexes beyond PKs.
mergedGaps.design: Generate drizzle/0000_baseline.sql from schema.ts. The runner (src/server/migrate.ts) takes an advisory lock and keeps schema_migrations(id,sha256,applied_at,app_version). A legacy install is accepted only if its structural fingerprint matches 0000. It runs a verified pre-migration backup, one transaction per file, then writes a SYSTEM_MIGRATION audit with actor migration:<os user>. A downgrade guard refuses to start on an unknown newer schema. Migration 0001 converts all timestamps to timestamptz and sets the DB zone to UTC (no production data exists yet, and audit hashes use timestamp_str). Then add counters and the index set. Split schema.ts into per-domain files, make protections a registry, and add GET /api/system/info. CI diffs the pg_dump of a fresh install against an upgraded one.
acceptance: A DB created from the v0.1.0 fixture upgrades with a valid audit chain, verifying signatures, a pre-migrate backup and a SCHEMA_MIGRATED audit row.
Under PGTZ=Africa/Cairo, DB-default and app-supplied timestamps read back with identical semantics.
CI fails when schema.ts changes without a migration, and an edited applied migration is refused by checksum.

Password login issues a fixed 8 h token, logout is a missing route, and the e-sig lockout (api.ts:257) becomes an indefinite login lock via api.ts:2217.

mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: oos_investigations has ten columns and no task, retest, impact or due-date structure. The Phase I checklist is Gemini text merged into free text. There is no retest linkage, no invalidation with an assignable cause and no retest limit. Close requires QA with no SoD against the investigator.
mergedGaps.design: Extend the oos tables: due_date, assignable_cause, decision, oos_tasks, oos_retests (plan approver, justification, retest_of) and checklist_templates. Phase I leads either to an assignable cause confirmed by QA (the original result is invalidated with a signed reason and a retest is authorised) or to Phase II, then a QA decision (Confirmed, Inconclusive, Invalidated) and a signed closure by QA who is not the investigator. A retest analyst != the original analyst and a maximum retest count are configurable settings. The AI checklist becomes an optional, labelled suggestion. Overdue investigations surface on the dashboard. Link a deviation via M27. Add an OOS vocabulary guard to the release blockers.
acceptance: Closing as Invalidated without an assignable cause, a QA signature and a linked retest is rejected, and closing by the assignee is rejected.
A retest by the original analyst is refused, and the third retest on a plan limited to two is refused.
A Phase I investigation past its due date appears as overdue.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 211.192, EU GMP Ch.6. Retesting and invalidation are the classic 'testing into compliance' finding, so every state change is signed and audited.

mergedGaps.title: QMS engine: deviation, CAPA, change control, audit findings [QA-10+QA-12 change control]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: Vault QMS, MasterControl and STARLIMS Quality Manager run configurable lifecycles with classification, action plans, effectiveness checks and links.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: There is no deviation, CAPA or change record anywhere (grep deviation|capa returns only UI labels and AI prompts). Traceability.tsx:822 asserts 'Zero Open OOS Investigations or Deviations', though no deviation can exist. No change control applies to specs, settings or roles. The compositeScore is invented (api.ts:1328-1336).
mergedGaps.design: qms_records (type, classification, state, owner, due, payload JSON validated by a per-type Zod schema, OCC), qms_actions (evidence ref and signature), qms_links, qms_comments (append-only) and qms_counters (FOR UPDATE). Per-type state machines through entityStates (Deviation: Draft, QA triage, Investigation, CAPA proposed, QA approval signed, Implementation, Effectiveness check, Closed signed). Major/critical needs a linked CAPA and an effectiveness check. Auto-open hooks in the originating transaction (EM excursion, confirmed OOS, instrument overdue use, backup fail, chain fail). A changeControlRequired setting gates spec approve, role raise and document effective with a CHANGE_REQUIRED error. Release blocker: open critical/major deviations.
acceptance: A major deviation cannot close without a linked CAPA and a QA signature.
Two simultaneous creations yield distinct ids. A CAPA action past due is flagged overdue.
Approving a spec without an Approved change request returns 409 when the setting is on. Editing a Closed record returns 423.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 211.192, 211.22, ICH Q10. A CAPA closed without effectiveness evidence is itself a finding. Enforcing change control is a documented setting with a signed emergency path.

mergedGaps.title: Controlled SOP/document lifecycle and training matrix with qualification gating [QA-08+QA-09]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: Vault QualityDocs and MasterControl run Draft, Review, Approved, Effective and Superseded with signed steps and periodic review. Vault Training assigns on effectivity. SampleManager and LabWare can block unqualified analysts.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: The schema has no documents table. The nav says 'SOP Training Matrix' but Training.tsx is one boolean (users.hasCompletedSoftwareTraining). Certify flips the global signing gate for any module (api.ts:1087). Overdue statuses come only from the seed. Result entry has no qualification check. ELN templates are unversioned.
mergedGaps.design: documents and document_versions (Draft, InReview, Approved, Effective, Superseded, Obsolete), files on disk by sha256, and a distinct author/reviewer/approver rule. Making a version Effective supersedes the previous one atomically (QA only). Controlled-copy footer and a print log. training_curricula, training_assignments (due, method, signature READ_AND_UNDERSTOOD by the trainee, OJT by a trainer != trainee) and analyst_qualifications. Assignments are auto-created when a version becomes Effective, and a scheduler marks Overdue. A result-guard QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED, with a QA override that is signed and flagged. The software-trained flag is derived and only the LIMS curriculum sets it.
acceptance: A version cannot become Effective without three distinct signatures and a QA role. Making v3 Effective supersedes v2 in the same transaction.
A 20 MB PDF uploads, and a tampered file fails the download with an audit row.
A user with an overdue mandatory assignment gets 403 QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED on result entry for that method.
Certifying a non-LIMS module no longer sets the global signing flag.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 211.100, 211.25, 11.10(i). Effective documents are immutable (triggers). The documents directory must be included in backup.

mergedGaps.title: Sample receipt, chain of custody, storage, aliquots, retain and labels/scanning [G8+G14+UX-08]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: LabWare Locations, STARLIMS Chain of Custody and SampleManager Inventory track receipt condition, holder, location hierarchy, aliquot lineage and retain/disposal. Wedge scanners work anywhere.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: samples has only id, material, batch, state, created_by, created_at, version. Nothing records receipt, holder, location, quantity or condition. The only scanner is a camera widget wired to the loaded list (Samples.tsx:74-83). No label generation exists. window.print appears only on two screens.
mergedGaps.design: A parallel custody status (no change to SampleState). storage_locations tree, sample_containers (child lineage), and custody_events (hash-linked ledger, trigger-protected, with qty balance). A sample_custody sidecar holds received_at, condition, mfg/exp, required_storage. A transition guard blocks Logged to Testing until received. Out-of-range temperature or a broken seal raises a deviation flag needing QA acknowledgement. Retain register with disposal due and a signed disposal. bwip-js (MIT) renders Code 128 and QR labels at @page size with window.print. label_prints is a hash-chained ledger and a reprint needs a reason. A global wedge-scan hook (bursts under 35 ms ending in Enter, ignored in inputs) calls GET /resolve?code=, which returns the record plus human-readable blockers (expired lot, overdue instrument). The camera scanner is a fallback.
acceptance: Begin Testing on an unreceived sample returns 400. Out-of-range receipt blocks testing until QA signs.
Aliquoting 5 mL from 20 mL creates a child and two ledger rows, the balance never goes negative, and UPDATE/DELETE on the ledger is refused.
Scanning a sample id anywhere opens it even if it is not in the loaded list, and an unknown code gives toast.error. A label reprint without a reason is refused.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 211.122-211.194, EU GMP Ch.6. A sample received out of temperature must not silently yield reportable data. The ledger is immutable, and mis-labelling is a mix-up risk.

mergedGaps.title: Reagent, reference-standard and solution lifecycle with usage-to-result link [G6]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: LabWare Inventory, SampleManager lot-controlled standards and STARLIMS Inventory manage lots, quarantine, in-use expiry, potency and consumption, and block expired material at result entry.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: One flat table reagents(name, lot, expiry text, status, quantity text) (schema.ts:124-131). There is no supplier, potency, retest, open date, consumption or parent/child. Nothing links a reagent to a result and expiry is not checked at entry. Dashboard counts are fixed in M13.
mergedGaps.design: reagent_items, reagent_lots (Quarantine to Approved needs a second person, in_use_expiry = min(expiry, opened + shelf life), potency with basis, retest_date), prepared_solutions (cannot outlive the parent), reagent_transactions (append-only ledger, balance >= 0) and result_materials. Receipt is e-signed. A result-guard rejects expired, retest-overdue, quarantined or rejected lots. A scheduler flips Expired and alerts at 30 and 7 days. A traceback query from a lot to every result.
acceptance: Saving a result that lists an expired or quarantined lot returns 400 naming the lot and date.
Opening a lot sets in_use_expiry, and a solution cannot expire after its parent.
reagent_transactions rejects UPDATE/DELETE. The lot traceback returns in under 1 s on 100k results.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 211.160(b)(4), 211.194(a)(2). The ledger is added to the trigger-protected list and to the OQ.

mergedGaps.title: Stability programme [G9 core]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: LabWare Stability, STARLIMS Stability Study Manager and SampleManager define protocols, compute pull calendars with windows, create pull samples and flag overdue pulls.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: pullPoints is hard-coded [1,3,6,9,12] (api.ts:2480) and the UI cannot change it. A study has no link to samples, results, specs or tests, and no due dates, chamber or overdue logic. PUT /stability lets anyone change product, batch and condition with the fixed reason 'User Update' (api.ts:2626-2654).
mergedGaps.design: stability_protocols (revision, signed, conditions JSON, month points, window), an ICH Q1A condition master (editable), stability_chambers, stability_timepoints (Scheduled, Due, Pulled, InTesting, Complete, Missed) and studies referencing protocol and batch. The scheduler marks Due and Missed (including start-up catch-up). Pull creates a normal sample through the same registration function with the test plan. A protocol change creates a new signed revision. PUT no longer edits product, batch or condition.
acceptance: 8 months × 2 conditions generate 16 timepoints with correct dates across month ends and leap years.
A timepoint turns Due and Missed with no user action, including after the PC was off.
Pull creates a sample with its stability_timepoint_id and the plan's result rows. Editing an Approved protocol returns 403/409.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 211.166, ICH Q1A. A missed pull is a deviation, not a silent edit.

mergedGaps.title: Environmental-monitoring programme [G10 full]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: LabWare/SampleManager/STARLIMS EM keep a site map of sampling points with per-grade and per-method alert/action limits, excursions, organism ID and adverse-trend rules.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: Location and grade are free text with no sampling-point master. Particle counts are never evaluated. PUT /env-records can change a count after the fact. The batch dossier attaches every EM record to every batch (api.ts:452-454).
mergedGaps.design: em_sampling_points, em_limit_profiles (editable, site-approved, source cited), em_results (media lot, incubation, organism, status server-set), and excursions opened in the same transaction through M27 hooks with batch impact by room and date window. Particle limits per ISO class. Adverse-trend rules (3 consecutive alerts, 2 actions in 30 days, recurring organism) evaluated by the scheduler, plus a dashboard heat grid. If the lab does not run aseptic work, scope this down to limits and trend.
acceptance: A client-supplied status is rejected by .strict(), and an Analyst changing a count gets 403.
3 consecutive alerts at a point are flagged as an adverse trend (fixture).
The batch dossier lists only EM results for the batch's rooms within its window.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022), 211.113(b). Limit tables are approved master data.

mergedGaps.title: Worklists and batch runs [G11]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: LabWare Worklists, STARLIMS Worklist and SampleManager group tests by method, instrument and analyst, export run sequences and show workload.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: Absent (grep worklist|assign in schema, api and components returns nothing). An analyst opens one sample at a time. Nothing enforces method training or prevents duplicate testing.
mergedGaps.design: worklists (WL-YYYY-NNNN counter, method, instrument, planned date, status) and worklist_items (position, kind Sample/Standard/Blank/SST/Control). A result_assignment sidecar. Item add rejects an assignee without the method training or an uncalibrated instrument. Release freezes membership, and later changes need a reason and are audited. CSV run sequence export and a PDF bench sheet through the job queue. Grid entry reuses saveResult per cell (OCC and audit per cell). A workload view. An assignment result-guard.
acceptance: Adding a result whose method the analyst lacks returns 400 naming the module.
After release, an item change without a reason is rejected and audited.
A non-assignee entering a result gets 403, and a 20-cell grid save yields 20 audit entries with a per-cell 409 on conflict.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 211.25 and Annex 11 s.12. Reuse of saveResult keeps one validated write path.

mergedGaps.title: Turnaround time and honest role-based KPIs [G13+UX-14]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: Incumbents track received, due and released timestamps with priority/SLA rules, alert on overdue, and report on-time %, aging, workload and OOS rate. Tiles drill into lists.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: There is no due date, priority or received timestamp. Dashboard figures are fixed in M13 only minimally. Metrics ignore Logged. 'Active OOS' counts status !== 'Closed' while nothing writes it (api.ts:1135). Pending Approvals disagrees between the tile and the chart. The audit-ready score is invented.
mergedGaps.design: A sample_tat sidecar (priority, due_at), a business calendar (weekend config, holidays), and time-in-state derived from the audit trail (Create/Transition rows). GET /metrics/tat and /kpi return SQL aggregates only: median and P90 cycle time, on-time %, aging buckets, OOS rate by parameter, right-first-time, instruments overdue, lots expiring, last verified chain and backup. Role-specific tiles, each a link to the exact filtered list. The scheduler raises due-in-24h and overdue events. Remove the invented score and the static validation claims, or show dated facts.
acceptance: A Thursday 16:00 receipt with a 2-business-day SLA and a Fri-Sat weekend is due Monday (table test).
Tile counts equal the row totals of the linked list. Closing an OOS reduces Active OOS by one.
The TAT endpoint matches hand-computed on-time % and P90 on a 10-sample fixture.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: Low direct risk, but fabricated values on a GxP screen are an ALCOA 'accurate' finding. Cycle time comes from the immutable audit trail.

mergedGaps.title: Audit-trail review workflow and tamper-evidence hardening [QA-07 rest+SEC-10]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: MHRA and PIC/S expect documented risk-based audit-trail review before release. Incumbents offer review-by-exception reports, and a keyed or anchored chain is rare.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: No audit review state exists and release does not require one. The hash is unkeyed SHA-256, so anyone with DB owner rights can rewrite and re-hash the chain, and the head anchor is manual. The app connects as the DB owner. The clock can be set back with no detection.
mergedGaps.design: audit_reviews (scope, seq range, reviewer != author of reviewed changes, AUDIT_REVIEW signature) and GET /audit/exceptions (edit after submit, SignatureFailed, role or setting change, same user created and approved). A release blocker when auditReviewRequiredForRelease. hash_alg 'hmac-sha256-v1' with the key from the keystore (v1 rows still verify). A daily HMAC-signed anchor file to a second path, and a start-up check of the chain tail against it. A CLOCK_ANOMALY event, with signing blocked until an admin acknowledges. A lims_app role with INSERT/SELECT only on audit_trail, signatures and security_events, no TRUNCATE, and ENABLE ALWAYS triggers, created from a boot step.
acceptance: As lims_app, update/delete on audit_trail and drop trigger fail with permission denied.
After rewriting and re-hashing the chain as owner, the anchor verify reports a mismatch.
Release returns 400 until an AUDIT_REVIEW covers the batch's rows, and a clock set back 10 minutes writes CLOCK_ANOMALY.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 11.10(e), Annex 11 s.9, PIC/S PI 041. The HMAC key is a new secret covered by the backup SOP. A hash change must keep v1 verification.

mergedGaps.title: Controlled release and update pipeline with integrity manifest [PLT-07+SEC-08 rest]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: Incumbents deliver signed, versioned packages with release notes and a delta validation pack, applied under customer change control.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: package.json has no publish block or updater. The version is 0.1.0 and asar:false leaves dist/** editable with no integrity check. CI builds an unsigned .exe but never installs it (DEV-06). Electron ^33 is outside the support window, xlsx@0.18.5 has known advisories, and actions are not pinned by SHA.
mergedGaps.design: Tag-derived versions. CI writes a signed release-manifest.json (hashes of dist, desktop, drizzle and the installer, git sha, schema version) and a CycloneDX SBOM. At start the app verifies dist/** against the manifest, refuses to run on a mismatch, and writes SERVER_START and SYSTEM_INTEGRITY_FAIL events. An electron-updater generic provider (LAN or UNC, autoDownload off) gated by an admin e-signature with a change reference, a verified pre-update backup and a SOFTWARE_UPDATED audit row, plus 'Install update from file' for air-gapped PCs. Authenticode signing when a certificate exists. A windows-latest job installs silently, boots, checks /api/ready and uninstalls. Upgrade Electron and pin actions.
acceptance: The About box shows the version, git sha and 'integrity OK'. One changed byte in dist/server.cjs blocks start and logs the file.
An update from v0.1.0 to v0.2.0 via UNC share leaves a verified backup and a SOFTWARE_UPDATED row.
The Windows CI job fails if /api/ready does not answer within 60 s. npm audit --omit=dev passes or has a recorded waiver.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: Annex 11 s.10 and 11.10(a). A signed manifest plus gated updates make the installed baseline provable. The Electron bump changes the validated runtime, so repeat the IQ.

mergedGaps.title: Validation automation and validated-scope control [PLT-06 rest+UX-10+QA-14]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: Vendors ship per-release validation packs with automated regression. Customers expect a clear validated scope.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: There is no frontend test. tests/ holds security-controls.sh, backup-restore.sh and a smoke test with a sandbox-only Playwright path (desktop-smoke.cjs:3). CI runs tsx server.ts against drizzle-kit push, not the shipped bundle and schema. RTM URS-005 is 'Pass' on API evidence only. DEV-2026-10-13-04 says ELN, OOS, stability, EM, reagents and others have no OQ and should be qualified or blocked in the UI, and nothing in the UI does.
mergedGaps.design: A Vitest suite replaces security-controls.sh, with the same OQ/GX/URS ids in the test names, and JUnit output feeding validation/build so the RTM and evidence are generated from executed tests. Playwright-Electron runs 12 flows (TOTP, session re-auth keeping typed value, register, OOS result, sign, close, calibrate, CoA, audit filter, scan simulation and keyboard-only), against a throwaway DB. An axe gate. A qualified_modules registry as middleware: a NotQualified module returns 403 MODULE_NOT_QUALIFIED and the UI shows a read-only badge. CI tests the shipped bundle and fails when a Critical/High URS has no executed test. A Windows job closes DEV-06.
acceptance: Reverting the Login TOTP fix turns the flow test red.
Marking a module NotQualified makes its writes return 403 MODULE_NOT_QUALIFIED. Changing the flag needs a QA e-signature.
The RTM links every Critical/High URS to an executed test id.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: GAMP 5 CSA risk-based assurance. A human must still countersign automated evidence, and nothing is marked Pass without an executed test.

mergedGaps.title: Arabic/English UI with RTL, locale-safe GxP dates and numbers, bilingual controlled print [UX-06+UX-05 Arabic]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: Incumbents ship translatable resources, and Arabic RTL quality varies and is usually a localisation project. Benchling is English-only, so a clean bilingual UI is a regional advantage.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: There is no i18n (lang='en' is hard-coded in index.html:2) and only Traceability.tsx has hard-coded Arabic. There are 74 physical-direction utilities across 17 files and 17 toLocale* call sites plus 4 split(',') hacks, which on an Arabic OS yield Arabic-Indic digits that Helvetica in jsPDF cannot draw. The Electron port is random, so localStorage is lost each launch.
mergedGaps.design: A dependency-free t() with src/i18n/{en,ar}.json. The language preference is stored server-side in users.preferences. Logical CSS utilities with rtl: variants, and <bdi dir=ltr> around ids, batches, hashes and values with units. src/lib/format.ts always formats Gregorian, Latin digits with the timezone shown, and toLocale* is banned by lint. Signature meanings are stored as codes with QA-approved translations, and the audit stays in canonical English. Bundled Arabic font. Bilingual controlled copies are rendered from the M25 snapshot through Chromium printToPDF. Add dark-mode tokens and a voice recogniser language.
acceptance: Switching to Arabic flips the shell to RTL with no horizontal overflow at 1024 px and persists after restart.
Ids, batches and hashes stay left-to-right in Arabic text.
On an Arabic-locale Windows PC every date prints as e.g. '13 Oct 2026, 12:12:00 GMT+3'. grep toLocale returns 0 outside format.ts.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: Regulated text must not change meaning in translation, so QA reviews the approved translations. Timestamps must stay unambiguous in every language.

mergedGaps.title: SPC, OOT and stability shelf-life trending [UX-11+QA-06 OOT+G9 trend]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: LabWare, STARLIMS, SampleManager and LabVantage include control charts with Westgard/Nelson rules, Cpk and baselines feeding APR and OOT alerts. Stability modules estimate shelf life per ICH Q1E.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: The only 'SPC' is a smoothed line chart with USL/LSL from row 0 and no mean, sigma or rules (Reports.tsx:500-561). /reports/trends includes unapproved and rejected samples, orders by sample creation rather than result time, loads all results and is O(S×R) (api.ts:1428-1475). There is no control-sample data model.
mergedGaps.design: spc.ts (pure, unit-tested): I-MR limits (2.66×MRbar), zones, rules (1>3σ, 2/3>2σ, 4/5>1σ, 8 same side, 6 trend), and Cpk only when n>=20 and both limits exist. ControlChart with linear lines, rule icons (not colour alone) and a tooltip deep link. The trends endpoint is rewritten as a single join over Approved samples, ordered by entered_at, with the spec as at entry, and unapproved data shown only on explicit opt-in with a hollow marker. control_limits are versioned and e-signed baselines. OOT alerts are evaluated after each approved result. Phase 2: qc_materials and Levey-Jennings with Westgard rules. Stability OLS regression with a one-sided 95% bound (ICH Q1E) from the stability tables.
acceptance: A 30-point seeded series matches hand-calculated CL/UCL/LCL within 1e-6.
A point at 3.2σ is flagged as rule 1, with smoothing off. Unapproved samples are excluded by default.
A baseline change needs a reason and e-signature and creates a new version. The stability regression matches a reference calculation to 3 decimals.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 211.180(e), EU GMP Ch.6. Limits must be reproducible and versioned. Any exclusion is explicit, justified and visible on the chart.

mergedGaps.title: Zero-install embedded PostgreSQL with least-privilege roles [PLT-04]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: Incumbents are installed by IT with a dedicated Oracle or SQL Server and DBA, owner and app accounts. A single-PC lab has no DBA, and SaaS vendors hide the database.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: desktop/setup.html:9-14 asks the user for an existing PostgreSQL. Nothing in the installer ships or supervises a database, and src/db/index.ts has no port option or timeouts. One role does DDL and requests. Installer and DPAPI paths were never run on the target PC (DEV-06).
mergedGaps.design: Ship PostgreSQL 16 Windows binaries as extraResources. First run: initdb in ProgramData with scram-sha-256, random passwords in safeStorage, listen 127.0.0.1 on a saved free port, timezone UTC, idle_in_transaction timeout, and the data directory restricted to the installing user. Roles lims_owner (DDL, migrations) and lims_app (DML, statement_timeout). The supervisor starts and polls pg_isready, restarts with backoff and stops gracefully. Setup offers 'Built-in database' (default) or 'Connect to existing'. A free-disk guard. Uninstall keeps pgdata unless the user opts in.
acceptance: On a clean Windows 11 VM with no PostgreSQL, install and first launch reach the login page with no database input.
Killing postgres.exe recovers within 15 s with no data loss, and quitting leaves no postgres.exe.
An existing PostgreSQL on 5432 does not conflict, and show timezone returns UTC.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: Record the bundled version and binary hashes in the IQ and release manifest. Least privilege strengthens the Annex 11 s.12 posture.

mergedGaps.title: Windows directory (LDAP/AD) sign-on with group-to-role mapping [SEC-14]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: LabWare, STARLIMS, SampleManager and LabVantage support AD/LDAP, and Vault, Benchling and MasterControl support SAML SSO. The directory usually owns lockout, expiry and joiner/mover/leaver.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: The only identity source is the local users table. No ldap, kerberos, saml or oidc code exists in src, server.ts, desktop or package.json.
mergedGaps.design: Add users.auth_provider and external_id. An LDAPS bind via ldapts (offline, LAN) with a stored CA. Search by UPN or sAMAccountName, bind as the user, and check userAccountControl, returning generic errors. ad_group_roles is re-evaluated at each login. The e-signature calls the same bind through the credentials service, with failures counted toward the local signing lockout. The local password policy UI is hidden for ldap users. A flagged local break-glass admin with MFA is allowed only when LDAP is unreachable, and every use is a security event. The bind password is encrypted by the keystore.
acceptance: An AD user logs in with the mapped role, and removal from the group removes it at next login.
A disabled AD account is refused at login and at e-signature.
With LDAP unreachable only the break-glass account works and each use is logged.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: 11.100/11.300 and Annex 11 s.12. The directory becomes part of the validation scope and needs IQ evidence of LDAPS certificate trust.

mergedGaps.title: Periodic review, retention, legal hold and batch archive [QA-13 rest+QA-03 access review]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: Enterprise LIMS/QMS provide periodic-review records for users, equipment and the system, retention classes with legal hold, and read-only batch archives.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: There is no periodic-review, retention, archive or legal-hold code (grep returns nothing relevant). There is no user-access review, and the restore drill is only automated by M14. Annex 11 s.11 and s.17 are unmet.
mergedGaps.design: periodic_reviews (user access, instrument, specification, document, system) with templates, due dates, findings and a signature. The user-access report lists users × role × last login × training. An annual system evaluation pack covers deviations, changes, backups, restore tests and audit-review coverage. retention_policies (conservative default) and legal-hold flags, with no purge function shipped. archiveBatch exports report PDFs, JSON of linked records, the audit slice and signatures, with a sha256 manifest, to a read-only ARCHIVE_DIR. verifyArchive re-hashes it, and archived records reject updates with 423.
acceptance: archiveBatch produces a bundle that passes verifyArchive, and one altered file fails it. Archived records return 423 on update.
A due user-access review shows on the QA dashboard, and completing it needs a signature.
A record class under legal hold cannot be flagged for purge.
mergedGaps.gxpRisk: Annex 11 s.11 and s.17, 211.180. Archive formats must stay readable (PDF plus open JSON), and legal hold blocks purge.

mergedGaps.title: Global search, code splitting and scale performance gate [UX-12+PLT-09 rest]
mergedGaps.competitorBenchmark: LabWare and STARLIMS offer a global find. Benchling's Cmd-K omnibar is the reference. Modern web LIMS code-split by module.
mergedGaps.currentStateEvidence: The production bundle is one 2.33 MB file (about 1.39 MB of it needed only after a click: html5-qrcode 368 KB, jsPDF and friends about 740 KB, xlsx 285 KB). App.tsx statically imports all 14 screens. There is no global search. /dashboard reads seven whole tables. The trends loop blocks the event loop for seconds at 10k samples (4.75 s measured).
mergedGaps.design: React.lazy per route with a chunk-error boundary that offers Retry. Dynamic import of jspdf, xlsx and the camera scanner, and d3 sub-packages only. manualChunks, with a first-load budget of about 700 KB. Ctrl+K opens GET /api/search?q=, which runs role-filtered ILIKE (and optional pg_trgm) across samples, batches, OOS, ELN, instruments, reagents and specs and excludes audit and admin data for non-privileged roles. Convert remaining findMany-then-filter paths to SQL aggregates. Add a tests/perf 100k-sample/400k-result/1M-audit seed with a nightly p95 gate and an EXPLAIN check.
acceptance: First-load JS is at most 700 KB raw, and jspdf, xlsx and html5-qrcode load only on first use.

verdicts.title: Platform core: api.ts split, transactional primitives, central validation and errors, test harness [PLT-03+SEC-06+PLT-06 harness]
verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
I could not refute the gap. A few partial pieces exist, but none of them does the job the gap names.

Already in the repo:
- **Partial split.** Only `src/server/reports.ts` (mounted at api.ts:1047 via `apiRouter.use(reportsRouter)`) and `src/server/workflow/transitions.ts` (`validateTransition`) are separate modules. The other 64 routes live in one `apiRouter`.
- **Audit primitive.** `src/db/utils.ts` has `writeAudit(tx, ...)`, which takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock(7001)` and writes the hash chain. api.ts calls it 32 times across 29 `db.transaction` blocks.
- **Unused wrapper.** `executeWithAudit` is defined at `src/db/utils.ts:82` but never called anywhere. There is no version-checked update helper such as `updateWithVersion`.
- **Partial central validation.** `src/lib/validations/lims.ts` holds `.strict()` Zod schemas. They are applied by per-route `safeParse` in 9 routes only (api.ts lines 1559, 1801, 1881, 2377, 2472, 2493, 2514, 2533, 2553). There is no validation middleware, and the notebook, ELN, training, admin, auth and other routes read raw `req.body`. The fix for GX-17 (Zod 4 error crash) was local to the sample registration route.
- **Per-route error handling.** Most handlers use a local `try/catch` that returns `res.status(400|500).json({error: e.message})`.
- **Check-then-write version checks.** About 7 routes read the row and compare `expectedVersion` in application code before updating. These are the ELN update at api.ts:205, results at 1818, sample transition at 1892, OOS close at 2399, and the OOS, stability, environment and specification PUTs at 2606, 2636, 2666 and 2714. None of them use `FOR UPDATE`, so a lost update is still possible under READ COMMITTED.
- **Test harness.** There is `tests/security-controls.sh` (90 lines of curl and psql black-box checks), `tests/backup-restore.sh` and `tests/desktop-smoke.cjs`. `.github/workflows/build.yml` runs lint, build, the OQ script and the backup script. There is no in-process unit or integration framework: no vitest, jest, supertest or `node:test`, no `*.test.*` files, and no `test` script in package.json other than `test:controls`.

Not present anywhere (grep of server.ts, src, tests, scripts and desktop):
- A 4-argument error middleware.
- `process.on('unhandledRejection')` or `process.on('uncaughtException')`.
- `express-async-errors` or any async-handler wrapper.

server.ts ends with `startServer().catch(console.error)`.

All cited numbers check out. Details and small corrections:

1. **Line count and routes.** `src/server/api.ts` is 3085 lines. It has exactly 64 `apiRouter.(get|post|put|delete)` declarations, plus `apiRouter.use(reportsRouter)` at line 1047. `POST /audit/verify` is declared twice, at lines 1979 and 2028. The second is dead code, because Express matches the first.

2. **Update calls.** There are exactly 27 `(tx|db).update(table).set(...)` calls (the other 10 grep hits for `.update(` are `createHash().update`). Every one uses an id-only `where`, including the multi-line ones at 310, 1842, 2418 and 2813. No `and(..., eq(x.version, ...))` appears anywhere in the file. The one `set` that bumps `version` (api.ts:1936, samples) still has `.where(eq(samples.id, ...))` only. This contradicts the AGENTS.md rule `WHERE id = $1 AND version = $2`. The statement holds as written, but about 7 of those updates are preceded by the non-atomic application-level check listed above.

3. **No error middleware.** Confirmed. server.ts has no 4-argument handler, so Express falls back to its default handler.

4. **Notebook crash.**
   - Express is 4.22.2 (package.json `^4.21.2`, node_modules 4.22.2), not 5. Express 4 does not forward rejected async handlers to `next`, so a thrown error becomes an unhandled rejection. Node 22.22.0 treats that as fatal.
   - The path is real. api.ts:1744 only checks `!password`, so `{"password":123}` passes. `verifyPassword` at 1754 then calls `scryptSync(123, ...)` (src/db/utils.ts:15-23), which throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`. All of this runs before the `try` that opens at 1762.
   - I reproduced it with a minimal Express 4.22.2 harness in the scratchpad. A POST with `{"password":123}` killed the process with "exit code 1" and an uncaught TypeError.
   - A non-string truthy `content`, such as `{"content":{}}`, also crashes. `content.trim()` at line 1741 runs outside the `try`.
   - The attacker only needs a valid authenticated session, so any user can take the server down.

5. **Same pattern elsewhere.** 18 handlers do `await` or other throwing work outside any `try`, or have no `try` at all, so each is a potential process-exit path. They include GET /training, GET /samples, GET /samples/:id, GET /audit and GET /audit/head, the stability, environment, specification, instrument and reagent GETs, and the pre-`try` parts of the POST /samples, results PUT, transition and OOS close routes.

verdicts.title: Desktop shell, server HTTP hardening, observability [SEC-07+SEC-11+PLT-08]
verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
The gap is mostly real, but four pieces of it are overstated or already covered.

1. The NODE_ENV and JWT-secret claim does not apply to the shipped desktop product.
- desktop/main.cjs:61 forks the server with NODE_ENV='production', so the Vite dev branch (server.ts:44) is never taken.
- main.cjs:62 passes JWT_SECRET=dec(c.jwtSecret). That secret is 48 random bytes generated at main.cjs:97 and stored encrypted with Electron safeStorage (DPAPI on Windows). main.cjs:20-26 refuses to store secrets in clear text.
- api.ts:30-32 throws if NODE_ENV=production and JWT_SECRET is unset. docs/gxp-audit-findings.csv records GX-01 as Fixed.
- tests/security-controls.sh checks that tokens signed with the old hardcoded secret are rejected.
- The public secret 'dev-only-insecure-jwt-secret' (api.ts:33) is reachable only when both NODE_ENV and JWT_SECRET are unset, for example `npm start` or `npm run dev` with nothing exported. CI sets JWT_SECRET (build.yml:27), so it does not hit this either.

2. A rate limiter exists and works against honest clients.
- server.ts:30-35 sets 200 requests per 15 minutes on /api.
- In my test with the same config, requests with no spoofed header were throttled as expected: 50 of 250 got 429.
- Separately, account lockout and signature lockout (GX-04, URS-006) limit password guessing no matter what the limiter does.

3. CSP is not entirely absent.
- helmet is on, with its other default headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, COOP, CORP, Referrer-Policy) present in the response I tested.
- desktop/setup.html carries a CSP meta tag (default-src 'self'), but that is the file:// setup window only.
- The main app (index.html) and public/backup.html have no CSP. backup.html uses an inline script.

4. The renderer is otherwise hardened.
- BrowserWindow uses sandbox:true, contextIsolation:true and nodeIntegration:false (main.cjs:84).
- setWindowOpenHandler denies new windows (main.cjs:86).
- The preload exposes only the config:get and config:save IPC calls.
- The server binds 127.0.0.1 on a random port (main.cjs:61).
- Socket.io CORS is disabled (GX-12).
- Operational output from init-db is captured and shown in the setup UI (main.cjs:52,99), but server output is not.

Confirmed items, with file:line evidence and what I ran. All cited line numbers match the code.

- **`npm start` has no NODE_ENV.** package.json:9 is `"start": "node dist/server.cjs"`. server.ts:44 takes the dev branch (`await import('vite')`) when NODE_ENV !== 'production', and api.ts:33 falls back to the public secret. This applies only to a non-desktop run without JWT_SECRET. The compiled dist/server.cjs keeps the same checks (lines 171394, 171397, 173992). server.ts:20 also defaults HOST to 0.0.0.0, so in that mode the server is network-reachable.

- **express.static serves the server bundle.** server.ts:53 does `app.use(express.static(distPath))` with no auth or filter. I mounted the real dist/ with the same config, and these all returned HTTP 200 unauthenticated:
  - /server.cjs (7,132,305 bytes)
  - /server.cjs.map (12,363,431 bytes)
  - /init-db.cjs
  - /backup-cli.cjs

  The build script (package.json:8) emits the sourcemap into dist/. In the desktop product the exposure is limited to local access on 127.0.0.1, because the port is random and loopback only.

- **CSP is off.** server.ts:26 has `contentSecurityPolicy: false`, with the comment "Disabled for Vite Dev Server compatibility". That applies in production too, and the test response had no content-security-policy header. A real CSP would have to allow the Google Fonts links in index.html and the inline script in backup.html.

- **trust proxy=1 makes the limiter spoofable.** server.ts:18 sets it, and nothing sets a keyGenerator, so the key is the IP only. With the same limiter config, 250 requests with a rotating X-Forwarded-For header were throttled 0 times (no spoofing: 50 of 250). The desktop has no reverse proxy, so the header is fully client-controlled.
  - Because every request reaches the server from 127.0.0.1, all application users on one PC share a single bucket. The bucket is per installation, not across PCs.
  - The limiter covers /api only.

- **The server child is forked silent with no log.** main.cjs:59-63 uses `silent: true`. Nothing reads server.stdout or server.stderr, and no log file is written (main.cjs:64 handles only 'exit'). The only failure message is a bare exit code or 'Server did not start' (main.cjs:38).

  - There is no request logging, health endpoint, Express error middleware, or uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handler.
  - There are only about 9 ad-hoc console.* calls on the server side.
  - The audit_trail table is GxP record auditing, not operational observability.
  - I did not verify a stall from the unread pipe. A 200,000-line test child completed normally.

- **will-navigate uses startsWith.** main.cjs:87 is `!(origin && u.startsWith(origin)) && !u.startsWith('file://')`.
  - `http://127.0.0.1:50000@evil.example/x` passes startsWith(origin), but new URL() reports the host as evil.example.
  - Any file:// URL is also allowed.
  - The Backup BrowserWindow created at main.cjs:73 has no will-navigate or window-open handler at all.

- **IDs.** SEC-07, SEC-11 and PLT-08 appear nowhere in the repo. They come from an external gap list, so I could not check wording against a source requirement.

verdicts.title: Versioned migrations, schema split, timestamptz fix, indexes [G2+QA-04+PLT-02+PLT-09 indexes]
verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
I could not refute the gap. The only schema-evolution machinery that exists is the following, and none of it is a versioned migration system.

1. Install path. `src/server/init-db.ts:20-27` checks `to_regclass('public.users')`. If the table is absent it runs every statement in `desktop/schema.sql`, split on `--> statement-breakpoint`. If the table is present it prints "Schema already present." and does nothing. This is a one-shot create with no upgrade path. A user on an older install who gets a new build never receives the new columns. `desktop/main.cjs:48-50` forks `dist/init-db.cjs` with `SCHEMA_FILE` set to that file.
2. Schema source of truth is split. `.github/workflows/build.yml:37` and `README.md:27` use `npx drizzle-kit push --config src/db/drizzle.config.ts`, which diffs `src/db/schema.ts` straight onto the database. The installer, `src/server/backup-cli.ts:23` (restore) and `init-db.ts` use the hand-kept `desktop/schema.sql`. CI therefore never tests the SQL file that ships.
3. Migration artefacts are absent. `src/db/drizzle.config.ts:17` sets `out: "./drizzle"`, but no `drizzle/` directory exists. A search of git history for deleted migration or `drizzle/` paths returned nothing. There is no `__drizzle_migrations` table, no `schema_version` or `schema_migrations` table, and no migrate runner anywhere in `src`, `server.ts` or `desktop`.
4. Ad hoc patching. `/home/user/taha/fix-db.ts` is an unversioned root script. It runs `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS totp_secret/totp_enabled`, and nothing in `package.json`, the workflows, `desktop` or the tests references it. The dozens of `patch-*.cjs` files at the repo root edit source code, not the database. The only repeated start-up DDL is `ensureProtections()` (`src/db/protections.ts`, called from `server.ts:21` and `init-db.ts:28`). It reinstalls only the audit_trail and signatures immutability triggers and has no versioning.
5. Timestamps. Every time column is `timestamp(...)` without a time zone (all 15 or so in `src/db/schema.ts`, and `timestamp` in `desktop/schema.sql`). Most are `.defaultNow()`, which stores `now()` as wall-clock time in the PostgreSQL session `TimeZone`. The pool (`src/db/index.ts:11-18`) sets no timezone option. Drizzle then reads the value back as UTC: `node_modules/drizzle-orm/pg-core/columns/timestamp.js:31` does `new Date(this.withTimezone ? value : value + "+0000")`. Values the app supplies from JS (`new Date()` at `src/server/api.ts:276/303/627/646`, `src/db/utils.ts:49`) are sent as UTC ISO strings, so DB-defaulted and app-supplied rows are inconsistent whenever the server zone is not UTC. No column uses `withTimezone`.
6. Indexes. There is no `CREATE INDEX` or `index()` / `uniqueIndex()` anywhere in `src`, `desktop/schema.sql` or the workflows. The only indexes are primary keys plus the three implicit indexes from UNIQUE constraints: `audit_trail.sequence` (`schema.sql:16`), `batch_releases.batch` (`:49`) and `users.uid` (`:225`). There are no indexes on foreign-key or lookup columns, although the code filters on them: `results.sampleId` and `signatures.sampleId` (`api.ts:134, 462, 481, 1414-1415, 1709-1711`), `signatures.timestamp` ordering, and `audit_trail` lookups by `entity_id`, `user_id` and `timestamp`. `writeAudit` finds the chain head with `ORDER BY sequence DESC`, which uses the unique index.

verdicts.correctedEvidence:
All claimed evidence checks out as stated:

1. **MFA bypass.** api.ts:2242 signs `{id, temp:true}` with the same `JWT_SECRET` as real sessions. `requireAuth` (api.ts:1101-1124) only does `jwt.verify` and looks the user up by `decodedToken.id`. It never inspects `.temp`. The only reads of `.temp` are api.ts:2267 and 2303, so a password-only tempToken works as a Bearer token on every `requireAuth` route for 5 minutes, and a new one can be requested at will.

2. **Plaintext `totpSecret` leak.** The column is plain text (schema.ts:17). `/training` (api.ts:1053) excludes only `passwordHash` and has no role check. `/admin/users` (api.ts:2968) blanks only `passwordHash` (Admin or QA). So any authenticated user, including a tempToken holder, can read every user's TOTP seed and generate their codes. No code in src ever writes `totpSecret`; it is only set by SQL in tests.

3. **Login.tsx field mismatch.** Login.tsx:56 tests `data.requireTotp`, but the server sends `requiresTotp` (api.ts:2243). A TOTP user falls into the final else and calls `onLogin(undefined, undefined)`, so the UI cannot complete MFA. The `requireTotpSetup` branch at line 52 is never triggered either.

4. **Missing routes.** There is no enrolment route and no change-password route. Nothing in src writes `passwordHash` (only seed_pg.ts and init-db.ts do) or `passwordChangedAt` (default only). The Admin UI password-policy fields (`minPasswordLength` and the require* flags) are therefore never enforced.

5. **Fixed 8 h token.** Password-only login uses `expiresIn: '8h'` at api.ts:2248, ignoring `sessionTimeoutMinutes`. Layout.tsx:36 POSTs `/api/auth/logout`, which has no route (it 404s). `fetch` does not throw on a 404, so the client logs out locally and the JWT stays valid until it expires, because there is no revocation.

6. **Lockout split.** The line 257 e-signature lock sets `lockedAt = now + 15 min` while the user stays `active`. The login check at api.ts:2217 is `!user.active || user.lockedAt`, which never compares the timestamp to now. So the e-signature lock becomes an indefinite login block. Details:
   - The login and e-signature paths share the same `failedAttempts` and `lockedAt` columns.
   - The e-signature threshold is hard-coded at 3 failures and 15 minutes, while login uses `settings.maxFailedLogins`.
   - The ELN sign success path (api.ts:264-266) resets `failedAttempts` but not `lockedAt`. The sample transition (api.ts:1931) and OOS close (api.ts:2413) paths do clear it.
   - Admin unlock via `PUT /admin/users/:id` clears `lockedAt` only on an inactive-to-active flip (api.ts:3003). An active but e-signature-locked user is therefore not cleared by an `active:true` call, and the admin must deactivate and then reactivate.
   - The login lock failure path sets `active=false` with `lockedAt=now` and writes no audit entry.

verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
Nothing in the gap exists. The client session layer is missing: there is no apiFetch wrapper, no idle lock or re-auth, no ErrorBoundary, no MFA enrolment, and no password-change screen. The only partial pieces are listed below.

- **Session-expiry check on reload only.** App.tsx:31-46 probes GET /api/samples when a stored token loads. On any non-ok response it clears gxp_token and returns to the login screen. This runs only on page load and is not a general 401 handler. Nothing else in src/ checks `.status === 401`.
- **Partial res.ok handling.** About 45 of the 68 fetch calls sit in files that check `res.ok`. Mutation handlers mostly do (for example `if (!res.ok) throw ...` followed by `toast(err.message, 'error')`). The read-on-mount GETs mostly do not.
- **Server-side session and password-expiry settings.** The server supports session timeout, lockout and password expiry. `sessionTimeoutMinutes`, `maxFailedLogins` and `passwordExpiryDays` are in schema.ts:155-157 and are editable in AdminPanel.tsx:322-356. totp-setup and totp-verify return `requiresPasswordChange` (api.ts:2291 and 2325). No client code reads that flag. Nothing in src/ enforces the idle timeout (client-side idle lock).
- **Login.tsx MFA UI.** Login.tsx:9-36 and 81-128 have a TOTP setup/verify form that posts to /api/auth/totp-setup and /api/auth/totp-verify. It cannot be reached or completed, as detailed in correctedEvidence.

verdicts.correctedEvidence:
Cited evidence checked against the code. Line numbers are slightly off but the substance holds.

**Confirmed**
- **Fetch count.** `grep "fetch("` over src finds 68 calls, not 67. It is 67 if App.tsx's probe is excluded. Every call is a raw fetch with a hand-built `Authorization: Bearer` header. The only wrapper-like code is Toast.tsx, and there is no apiFetch anywhere.

- **Reagents.tsx:19-22 (cited 18-22).** The same pattern. `setReagents({error})` makes `reagents.filter(...)` at line 46 throw. The swallowed `.catch(() => {})` also hides network errors.
- **No ErrorBoundary.** Grep for ErrorBoundary, componentDidCatch and getDerivedStateFromError returns nothing. main.tsx renders `<App/>` bare in StrictMode, so any render throw unmounts the whole app.
- **App.tsx:35 (exact).** `JSON.parse(atob(token.split('.')[1]))` decodes base64url as Latin-1. UTF-8 names such as Arabic come out garbled, and base64url `-` or `_` characters throw. The catch at line 37-38 silently substitutes `{name:'System User', role:'Analyst'}`. That is a GxP attribution problem and a silent failure under the AGENTS.md rule. It also fabricates the Analyst role in the UI.
- **Layout.tsx:36 (exact).** `fetch('/api/auth/logout', {method:'POST'})`. api.ts has no logout route (the only /auth routes are login-local, totp-setup and totp-verify), and no other file in src/ or server.ts contains "logout". Express returns 404. fetch does not reject on 404, so the client logs out anyway and shows "Logged out successfully", but the server records no logout. The call also sends no Authorization header.
- **Static badges.** Layout.tsx:148-151 shows "21 CFR Part 11 Validated" with a pulsing green dot, and line 152-154 shows "ALCOA+ Compliant". Dashboard.tsx:40 has a second "21 CFR Part 11 Validated" badge, which the claim missed. All are hard-coded and not tied to any validation state. Login.tsx:78 adds "21 CFR Part 11 Compliant Authentication".

**"Login.tsx cannot complete MFA" is true, but the real cause is not a missing UI**
- The server's login-local returns `{ requiresTotp: true, tempToken }` (api.ts:2243). Login.tsx:52-58 checks `data.requireTotpSetup` and `data.requireTotp`. Those names do not match, so the verify step never opens. A TOTP-enabled user falls into the final else branch and runs `onLogin(undefined, undefined)`. That stores the string "undefined" as gxp_token, shows an "Authentication Successful" toast, and then App.tsx sends the user back to the login form.
- No endpoint ever returns `requireTotpSetup` or `qrCode`. `generateSecret` and `QRCode` are imported at api.ts:1-2 but never used. Nothing sets `totpSecret`. totp-setup at api.ts:2270 requires `user.totpSecret` to already exist, so enrolment is impossible through the app.

**Related gaps that fit the same item**
- There is no password-change screen and no password-change endpoint. The only user mutation is PUT /admin/users/:id. `requiresPasswordChange` is computed server-side and ignored by the client.

verdicts.title: E-signature service: polymorphic binding, meaning catalog, snapshots, uniform failure handling [QA-01+SEC-05 esign+PLT-03 signedAction+G3 polymorphism]
verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
The gap is real: nothing in the code is a shared e-signature service, a polymorphic binding or a meaning catalog that signing uses. Every concrete claim holds up, apart from one count and one nuance, but some pieces exist and one path is already fixed.

**What exists already (the claim leaves these out):**
- The sample transition path (POST /samples/:id/transition, api.ts:1873-1972) already handles failure properly. It records `signatureFailure` inside the transaction, then commits the counter, the 15-minute lock and the `SignatureFailed` audit in a separate transaction in the catch block (api.ts:1964-1969). It also enforces training (1920), checks the lock (1877) and hashes the content (1941). The project's own finding GX-04 (docs/gxp-audit-findings.csv:5) fixed this for the sample path only.
- A meaning catalog exists for sample transitions: `SampleWorkflow[].signatureMeaning` in src/server/workflow/transitions.ts:27-63. It is dead on the server. `validateTransition` is called at api.ts:1898, but `verdict.signatureMeaning` is never read. api.ts:1938-1940 uses different hard-coded strings instead, for example 'Approval (Release Disposition)' against the catalog's 'Approval of Results - Batch Release'.
- DB-level append-only triggers on `signatures` and `audit_trail` exist (src/db/protections.ts), including a guard that allows the one-time 'pending' to audit-id link.
- Most signature rows carry a SHA-256 `contentHash`.
- ELN sign (api.ts:252-262) persists a failed-attempt counter and a 15-minute lock outside any transaction. It writes no `SignatureFailed` audit.
- ElectronicSignatureModal.tsx:97 blocks untrained users on the client, but only on the client.

**What is missing (verified):**
- There is no entity-type column and no polymorphic binding on `signatures`. `sample_id` is NOT NULL with an FK to samples (schema.ts:66). The FK is real in the installed DDL (desktop/schema.sql:243), and init-db.ts applies that file on a fresh install.
- There is no shared e-sign function. Six handlers insert signature rows inline: ELN, release, notebook, sample transition, OOS close and spec approve. Calibrate and certify check the password and write no signature row at all.
- Meanings are hard-coded strings in the server, or come from the client body (ELN: `meaning || default` at api.ts:293).
- Only the sample path can recompute a content hash (api.ts:2146-2155).
verdicts.correctedEvidence:
**Confirmed, with exact lines:**
- **Schema.** schema.ts:66 is `sampleId: text('sample_id').references(() => samples.id).notNull()`.
- **Spec approve.** api.ts:2774 inserts `sampleId: spec.id`, with the comment "Using sampleId col for generic entity ID mapping ... in this MVP". I ran desktop/schema.sql on a scratch Postgres 16 (since removed). Inserting `sample_id='SPEC-1'` failed with `signatures_sample_id_samples_id_fk ... Key (sample_id)=(SPEC-1) is not present in table "samples"`.
- **Why a fresh install is stuck.**
  - Registering a sample needs an Active spec (api.ts:1579-1584).
  - POST /specifications creates only Draft (2512-2530).
  - Draft to Active happens only in approve.
  - init-db.ts seeds no specs. Only the demo seeder seed_pg.ts inserts Active specs directly.
  - No test or validation script exercises spec approve.
  - Approve therefore always fails with a 500 on a fresh install, and the transaction rolls back.
- **ELN fallback.** api.ts:299 is `existing.sampleId || existing.id`. `lab_notebook.sample_id` is nullable (schema.ts:169) and POST /eln stores `sampleId || null` (api.ts:166), so an ELN with no sample hits the FK on sign. The UI always sends a sample, defaulting to the hard-coded seed ID 'SMP-2026-00001' (ELN.tsx:30,182), so this path is reachable mainly through direct API calls.
- **Release fallback.** api.ts:642 is `sampleIds[0] || batch`. The batch name is used only for a batch with no samples. Otherwise the release signature is bound to the first sample alone.
- **Rollback of failure bookkeeping.** In OOS close, the counter update (api.ts:2409) and the `SignatureFailed` audit (2410) sit inside `db.transaction`, then 2411 throws, so both roll back. The catch at 2464 has no compensating write. The claim cites 2408-2411, and the counter update is at 2409. Spec approve writes `SignatureFailed` at 2742 and throws at 2743, so it rolls back. It has no counter or lock check at all.
- **No failure tracking at all.**
  - Release: 609-612 returns 401 with nothing recorded.
  - Calibrate: 2802-2804, same.
  - Certify: 1068-1070, same.
  - Notebook: 1754-1760, whose own comment says lock tracking is omitted.
- **Notebook hash.** api.ts:1778 inserts `contentHash: 'N/A', auditEntryId: 'N/A'`. The audit written at 1782 is never linked.
- **Training enforcement.**
  - Enforced on 4 paths: ELN (242), release (604), sample transition (1920) and OOS close (2388).
  - Not enforced on notebook, spec approve, calibrate and certify.
  - Certify is exempt by design under the AGENTS.md bypass rule.
  - The sample-path check carries a dead exemption, `newState !== 'some_training_state'`.
- **Meanings.** ELN accepts a client-supplied `meaning`. Every other path hard-codes it. The notebook UI shows "Authorship & Integrity of Analytical Observations" (SampleDetail.tsx:635), while the server stores 'I am the author of this observation'.
- **Verify endpoint.** `contentHashMatches` stays null unless the audit entry is a Sample `Transition` (api.ts:2146-2155). The response is `valid: chainValid && contentHashMatches !== false` (2159), so null means valid. ELN, release, OOS, spec and notebook signatures can never fail the hash check, and a notebook row with 'N/A' verifies as valid.

**Corrections to the claim:**
1. The path count is off. api.ts has 8 password-gated e-signature endpoints (ELN, release, certify, notebook, sample transition, OOS close, spec approve, calibrate). Admin settings, admin user update and backup also re-ask for the password, making 12 in all. I could not reproduce "9". The finding that exactly 4 enforce training stands.
2. Sample transition is a working reference implementation and should not be described as broken.
3. Spec approve has other gaps the claim does not mention: no role check, no lock check, and no `expectedVersion` check.

- POST /samples/:id/transition (1873-1966) enforces role per transition and SoD. `validateTransition` is in src/server/workflow/transitions.ts:77. It also enforces e-signature password, training guardrail, lockout, and an enteredBy-based SoD at approve/reject.

Correct isOos readers exist: pdfWorker.ts:45 (server-side PDF), Traceability.tsx:163 and 703, and the /reports/trends payload (api.ts:1464).

Not present anywhere (grep and reading found nothing):
- Any numeric/qualifier parser: no handling of '<', '>', 'ND', 'BLQ', thousands separators or strict numeric validation. `resultUpdateSchema` (src/lib/validations/lims.ts:8) accepts any non-empty string.

It takes sampleId/resultId/parameter/dateRaised straight from `req.body`, with no Zod schema, no role check, and no check that resultId belongs to sampleId or is actually OOS. The UI's handleCreateOOS (OOSInvestigations.tsx:52+) is the only caller. The result PUT never creates an investigation.

verdicts.title: Specification lifecycle: author, revision vs OCC, effective date, SoD approval, sample binding [G3 part+QA-12 spec]
verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
The gap is real: I found no author column, no separate revision field, no effectiveDate logic, no approver role/training/SoD check, and no spec binding on samples. I read the DDL and code but did not run the app or a database.

What already exists, none of which closes the gap:
- Status machine Draft -> Active -> Obsolete. PUT is limited to Draft (api.ts:2713) and approve to Draft (api.ts:2749). Approving a spec also marks the previous Active spec for the same material Obsolete, with an audit row per change (api.ts:2751-2758).
- Audit rows are written in the same transaction for create (api.ts:2524), parameter update (api.ts:2722), supersede (api.ts:2757) and approve (api.ts:2766). An author is therefore recoverable indirectly from the 'Create' row's userId, but it is not a column and nothing uses it.
- POST /specifications uses a .strict() Zod schema (lims.ts:47-51).
- PUT compares expectedVersion to the stored version inside the transaction (api.ts:2708, 2714). The UpDATE's WHERE clause is only on id (api.ts:2721), not `id AND version`, which AGENTS.md requires.
- Approve re-verifies the signer's password (api.ts:2739-2744) and tries to insert a signature row with meaning 'Master Data Approval', recordVersion and contentHash (api.ts:2772-2781). That insert cannot succeed (see the FK point below).
- The Approve and Create controls are hidden from non-QA/Admin users in the UI only (Specifications.tsx:131, 195).
- POST /samples requires an Active spec for the material and copies specMin/specMax onto each result row (api.ts:1579-1600). That copies the limits only and does not record which spec produced them.
verdicts.correctedEvidence:
Every sub-claim checks out against the code. Detail per sub-claim:

1. Revision and OCC share one column. The `specifications` table has only id, material, version, effective_date, status and parameters (schema.ts:108-115; desktop/schema.sql:168-175). The PUT bump is `version: existing.version + 1`. That is at api.ts:2718, not 2717; line 2717 is `parameters: parameters`. The approve bump is at api.ts:2763 and is correct. The UI sends `expectedVersion: editingSpec.version`, with a comment saying it is the same column (Specifications.tsx:72). Create stores the user-typed version (api.ts:2521). A v1 edited once and approved becomes 3, and the UI renders `v{spec.version}.0` (Specifications.tsx:160) as "v3.0". Nothing enforces unique or monotonic revisions per material. Obsoleting the old Active spec does not bump its version (api.ts:2756).

2. There is no author column. A grep of the schema and DDL finds no createdBy or author on specifications. The samples table does have createdBy; specifications does not.

3. PUT parameters is unvalidated. api.ts:2705 destructures `req.body` directly with no Zod. The only check is `typeof expectedVersion === 'number'`, so any JSON can be stored in the jsonb column. This also violates the AGENTS.md rule requiring .strict() Zod on all inputs.

4. effectiveDate is never evaluated. A grep finds it only in the create insert (api.ts:2516, 2521), the Zod string check (lims.ts:50), the type definition (types.ts:89), the seed data and a display line (Specifications.tsx:193). The Active lookups at api.ts:1579-1581 and 1642-1644 filter only on material and status. A future-dated spec is therefore used as soon as it is approved. The date can be any non-empty string, since the schema only checks `min(1)`.

5. Approve has no role, training or SoD check. api.ts:2731-2789 uses only `requireAuth`. There is no role check and no `hasCompletedSoftwareTraining` check. There is no check that the approver differs from the author. By contrast, the sample-transition, batch-release and OOS-close handlers do have these checks (api.ts:242, 604, 1920, 2388). Create (api.ts:2512) and PUT (api.ts:2702) also have no role check.

6. The FK failure is real. The approve handler inserts into `signatures` with `sampleId: spec.id` (api.ts:2774). `signatures.sample_id` has a foreign key to `samples.id` (schema.ts:66; desktop/schema.sql:243). A `SPEC-xxxx` id cannot satisfy it, so approving any spec through the API rolls back the whole transaction and returns 500. Only the seeded Active specs exist. I could not find the M07 reference in the repo outside the Word documents, which I did not open, but the failure itself is real.

7. Samples store no spec id or revision. The samples table has id, material, batch, state, createdBy, createdAt and version. The results table has specMin and specMax but no spec reference. The match is exact and case-sensitive: `eq(t.material, material)` (api.ts:1579-1581), repeated in bulk import (api.ts:1642-1643). The Zod schema does no trim or normalisation (lims.ts:3-6). "paracetamol 500mg" will not match "Paracetamol 500mg".

verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
All five sub-claims are real. Every cited file:line points at the code described. The following controls exist, but none of them closes the gaps.

- Sign (src/server/api.ts:231-355): requires authentication and a password, which is re-verified with scrypt. It enforces the training guardrail (:242), a 3-failure/15-minute lockout (:246-261) and an already-signed/locked check (:270). It writes a signature row with recordVersion, a SHA-256 contentHash and a hash-chained audit entry in one transaction, and back-links auditEntryId (:334). GET /eln/:id/verify exists (:357).
- PUT /eln/:id (:192-229): refuses edits to Signed or locked records (:201), has an optional expectedVersion check done in application code (:205), and writes an audit in the same transaction.
- writeAudit (src/db/utils.ts): serialises writers with an advisory lock and builds a sha256 chain (sequence, prevHash, hash). It does not truncate values itself.
- Sample-notebook POST (:1736-1791): takes a password, verifies it, writes the audit entry in the transaction and stores a signature row. The full content goes into the audit (:1782). The UI hides the entry form when the sample is Approved or Rejected, and for non-Analyst/Admin roles (src/components/SampleDetail.tsx:288, ~477).
- The ELN UI sends only {password} when signing (src/components/ELN.tsx:119-123), so the client does not normally supply a meaning. Only the API accepts one.

None of these is a server-side control for the gaps below. No DB trigger or constraint covers lab_notebook or notebook_templates (checked desktop/schema.sql). Nothing outside api.ts mounts or wraps the ELN routes (server.ts:41 only mounts apiRouter).

Verified claims, all with accurate line numbers:

1. ELN sign accepts a client meaning and has no author check. :233 destructures `{ password, reason, meaning }` from req.body. :293 uses it as `signMeaning = meaning || 'Authorship & Verification...'`, stored at :301 and :314. Nothing between :268 and :318 compares `existing.enteredBy` with `user.id`, and there is no role check. Any authenticated, trained user can therefore sign someone else's worksheet with the meaning 'Authorship' or any free text. Related defects in the same handler:
   - The UPDATE at :310-318 has `WHERE id` only, with no `AND version`. This breaks the AGENTS.md OCC rule.
   - The "already signed" check at :270 happens outside the transaction, so two concurrent signs can race.
   - `signatures.sampleId` is `existing.sampleId || existing.id` (:299), but signatures.sample_id is NOT NULL with an FK to samples (schema.ts:66; desktop/schema.sql:243). Signing a standalone worksheet with no sampleId would insert 'ELN-XXXX' and very likely fail the FK and return 500. I inferred this from the DDL and did not run it.

2. PUT /eln/:id has no author check (:192-229). No comparison of `existing.enteredBy` and `user.id`, and no role check. Also:
   - `expectedVersion` is optional (:205 only checks `!== undefined`).
   - The UPDATE at :220 has `WHERE id` only, with no version predicate.
   - There is no Zod schema; fields come straight from req.body.

3. The audit truncates old/new to 100 chars (:221): `existing.content.substring(0,100)` and `updates.content.substring(0,100)`, with field fixed as 'content'. Title, sampleId, experimentType and pharmacopeia changes are not audited (:211-218). A title-only edit logs identical old and new content. The hash chain therefore covers truncated data, and the prior version cannot be reconstructed.

4. Template create has no role or audit (:3031-3048). It is requireAuth only, so any user can create templates. It does a bare `db.insert` with no transaction and no writeAudit, uses a Math.random id (:3038), has no Zod validation, and the table has no version column (schema.ts:184-189). There is no update or delete route and no approval or versioning, so templates are uncontrolled content that gets pasted into GxP records.

5. The sample notebook accepts entries on Approved samples and stores contentHash 'N/A' (:1736-1791). The transaction only checks that the sample exists (:1764-1765), with no `sample.state` check (compare :1810 in the results PUT). The only guard is client-side (SampleDetail.tsx:288). :1778 hardcodes `contentHash: 'N/A', auditEntryId: 'N/A'`; the writeAudit return value at :1782 is discarded, so the signature is not linked to the audit. Further defects at the same location:
   - The labNotebook insert (:1770) sets no status, locked or contentHash, so rows default to status 'Draft' and locked=false with a null contentHash. The UI shows an "E-Signed" badge on every entry unconditionally (SampleDetail.tsx ~464). Such an "e-signed" observation can still be edited through PUT /eln/:id, or re-signed.
   - There is no hasCompletedSoftwareTraining check, unlike /eln/:id/sign (:242), and no server-side role check.
   - Failed passwords at :1756-1759 are not counted toward lockout (the code comment says so), so this is a password-guessing oracle.
