verdicts.title: Backup v2: streaming, text-exact timestamps, scheduled with mirror, retention, restore drills [PLT-01+QA-13 backup+SEC-10 scheduler]
verdicts.id: Backup v2: streaming, text-exact timestamps, scheduled with mirror, retention, restore drills [PLT-01+QA-13 backup+SEC-10 scheduler]
verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
I could not refute the gap. Backup v1 exists and works, but none of the v2 capabilities do. Every cited fact checked out, and I reproduced the timestamp bug end to end.

What exists today:
- src/server/backup.ts is an encrypted logical backup: AES-256-GCM with a scrypt-derived key.
- It takes one REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY snapshot.
- It writes a manifest with row counts, a data hash and the audit head.
- It self-verifies right after writing (backup.ts:84).
- verifyBackupFile re-checks the data hash, row counts and the audit hash chain.
- restoreBackup only restores into an empty database, then re-installs the immutability triggers.
- There are two manual entry points:
  - POST /api/admin/backup and POST /api/admin/backup/verify (api.ts:3065-3083). They are Admin-only and require password re-entry. They write BACKUP_CREATED and BACKUP_VERIFIED audit events.
  - A CLI, src/server/backup-cli.ts, with backup, verify and restore. It reads the passphrase from the BACKUP_PASSPHRASE environment variable, so an OS scheduler could call it, but nothing in the product does.
- The only UI is public/backup.html and the desktop menu item "Backup…" (main.cjs:73).
- tests/backup-restore.sh runs as OQ-09 in CI. It does one restore into a throwaway database per push. That is a validation test, not a restore drill of a real backup. Evidence is in validation/evidence/backup-run-2026-10-13.txt.
- The audit chain already uses a text timestamp (audit_trail.timestamp_str), and verifyAuditChain prefers it (backup.ts:26). The chain is therefore immune to the timestamp shift. The bug affects the naive `timestamp` columns only, and that includes audit_trail.timestamp.

What does not exist, searched in src, server.ts, desktop, package.json, tests, .github and the docs:
- Scheduler: node-cron is not in package.json or node_modules. AGENTS.md lists it as a core technology, but it is not a dependency. There is no cron or setInterval for backups. The only setInterval is the RabbitMQ local queue poll (rabbitmq.ts:38).
- Mirror or off-disk copy: none. public/backup.html:5 only tells the user to copy the file to a share by hand.
- Retention or pruning: none. No rotate, prune or retention code.
- Automated restore drills: none.
- Streaming: none.
- Text-exact timestamp handling: none. There is no setTypeParser or pg.types override anywhere, and no timestamptz column in src/db/schema.ts or desktop/schema.sql.
verdicts.correctedEvidence:
Every claimed item is accurate. Corrections and additions:

1. Manual backups (DEV-2026-10-13-08). Confirmed at validation/docs/deviations.csv:9 (also in validation/build/content.cjs:116). RTM.csv:27 says "Manual backup/verify/restore only; scheduling and off-PC copy are procedural (DEV-08)".

2. Same disk (main.cjs:62). Exact. The line sets BACKUP_DIR to path.join(app.getPath('userData'), 'backups'). The server fallback is process.cwd()/backups (api.ts:3068). A stray `backups/` folder with three .bak files already sits in the repo root; it is gitignored.

3. Passphrase typed per request. Confirmed:
   - api.ts:3068 reads `req.body.passphrase`.
   - public/backup.html has a passphrase input.
   - The CLI needs the BACKUP_PASSPHRASE environment variable.
   - There is no stored key or key reference.

4. Memory. In createBackup, `select *` runs on every table into one in-memory object (backup.ts:73). JSON.stringify is called twice there: once for dataHash at :77 and once inside seal at :54. It then gzips synchronously and writes the file.
   - It is worse than "twice". createBackup immediately calls verifyBackupFile (:84), which does readFileSync, decrypts, JSON.parse, and a third JSON.stringify(p.tables) (:93).
   - restoreBackup repeats verify and open, so the whole payload is held and stringified several more times.
   - Node 22.22.0 reports buffer.constants.MAX_STRING_LENGTH = 536870888 (about 512 MiB). In my test, a stringify past that threw `RangeError: Invalid string length`, so the claim holds.

5. Timestamp shift. Confirmed with the real backup.ts against a throwaway Postgres 16. I used the actual createBackup and restoreBackup, with desktop/schema.sql as the target schema. The test rows were users.created_at, signatures.timestamp and samples.created_at, all set to '2026-10-13 10:00:00.123'.

   | Machine TZ | Restored value | Shift | verified | countsMatch | chainIntact |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | UTC | 10:00:00.123 | none | true | true | true |
   | Africa/Cairo | 07:00:00.123 | -3h | true | true | true |
   | America/New_York | 14:00:00.123 | +4h | true | true | true |

   - Why it happens: backup.ts runs the query on a raw pg client (`c.query`), not through drizzle. Drizzle installs raw-string timestamp parsers only for its own queries. The raw client therefore uses pg-types' parseDate, which builds a local-time Date for OID 1114. JSON.stringify then writes that Date as a UTC ISO string ending in 'Z'. restoreBackup passes that string as a bind parameter (backup.ts:120-121). A `timestamp without time zone` column drops the 'Z', so the stored value is the original wall-clock value shifted by the machine's UTC offset, and the offset is DST-dependent.

verdicts.title: Durable job queue and start-up catch-up scheduler [G2 scheduler+PLT-11+QA-13 scheduler]
verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
Nothing that closes the gap. I tried to refute each sub-claim and none was refuted. These are the only partial mitigations I found.

1. Durable queue pieces (src/server/rabbitmq.ts):
- publishTask inserts a `jobs` row before sending (lines 45-50).
- The AMQP path asserts a durable queue and publishes with persistent:true (lines 16 and 53).
- This is the "durable job" part. It has no reclaim or catch-up.

2. In AMQP mode, an unacked message is redelivered after a crash, so a crashed job re-runs. This is broker behaviour, not code. The local fallback has nothing equivalent.

3. Instrument calibration "Overdue" is computed at read time from calibrationDueDate (src/server/api.ts:1147-1150). That is not a scheduler, and it does not apply to training.

4. Encrypted backup and verify exist (src/server/backup.ts, backup-cli.ts, POST /admin/backup at api.ts:3065). They run only on manual or CLI calls. The audit text says 'Scheduled/manual backup' (api.ts:3070), but nothing schedules them.

5. src/lib/queue/rabbitmq.ts is a second, unrelated queue module. It is dead code: the only reference is a commented-out import at api.ts:35.
verdicts.correctedEvidence:
All six sub-claims check out. Notes on precision:

- **Polling:** src/server/rabbitmq.ts:38 has `setInterval(processLocalQueue, 5000)`. processLocalQueue (lines 59-72) does `findMany({where: status='pending', limit: 1})`. That is a plain SELECT with no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and no atomic claim, so it is check-then-act. Two instances or ticks can pick the same row. Only the later status flip to 'processing' (line 75) narrows the window.

- **Re-entrancy:** there is no flag, mutex or in-flight guard on the async interval callback.

- **Crashed 'processing' rows:** the poller selects only 'pending' rows. The only reference to 'processing' in the server is the write at line 75. So a row left in 'processing' by a crash is never retried, in the local fallback or anywhere else. Pending rows are also never recovered when RabbitMQ is up: the poller is not started in AMQP mode, so a crash between the insert (line 45) and sendToQueue (line 53) orphans the job.

- **Poison loop:** `channel!.nack(msg)` at line 30 passes no requeue argument. amqplib 2.0.1 defaults it to true (node_modules/amqplib/lib/api_args.js:273). Note that processJob (lines 74-85) catches its own errors and writes 'failed', so the consumer's catch fires only for a malformed JSON message or a DB failure on the status update. Those cases requeue forever, with no retry cap, dead-letter queue or prefetch.

- **Job ids:** line 43 is `job-${Math.random().toString(36).substr(2, 9)}`. There is no uniqueness retry.

- **/reports/status/:jobId** (src/server/reports.ts:22-38):
  - It has requireAuth only. It returns `job.result` for any authenticated user and does no ownership or role check.
  - The `jobs` table (src/db/schema.ts:132-140, also desktop/schema.sql:73-81) has no userId or createdBy column, so ownership cannot be checked without a schema change.
  - The result is the full Certificate of Analysis from `doc.output('datauristring')` (pdfWorker.ts:~100), a base64 data URI.
  - POST /reports/generate (reports.ts:10-20) also has no Zod `.strict()` validation, no role or sample access check, and no audit-trail entry. This breaks the AGENTS.md rules.

- **node-cron:** it is absent from package.json, package-lock.json and node_modules. The only mentions are AGENTS.md lines 10 and 28. The only timer in server code is the rabbitmq.ts:38 `setInterval`. server.ts calls only `ensureProtections()` and `initRabbitMQ()` at startup, with no catch-up.

- **Training 'Overdue':** the only places 'Overdue' appears are the seed rows (src/server/seed_pg.ts:613, 615, 618) and read-only filters and counters in api.ts:1265, 1277, 1289. The only runtime write to training_records.status is 'Completed' (api.ts:1081). training_records (schema.ts:143-151) has no dueDate or expiry column, and the schema comment lists only "Pending, Completed". Nothing can ever transition a record to Overdue, so the dashboard's overdue-training widgets show only seeded data.

verdicts.whatAlreadyExists:
I found no methods, test plans, calculation engine or system suitability (SST) logic anywhere in code, schema or UI. I only found these small neighbouring pieces, none of which closes the gap.

1. Specs hold a JSONB list, and nothing normalises it.
- `specifications.parameters` is `jsonb('parameters').$type<any[]>()` at `src/db/schema.ts:108-115`, with the same shape in `desktop/schema.sql:168-175`.
- There is no parameters table and no method table. The 18 tables in `schema.ts` are users, samples, results, audit_trail, signatures, oos_investigations, stability_studies, env_records, specifications, instruments, reagents, jobs, training_records, system_settings, lab_notebook, notebook_templates, batch_materials and batch_releases.
- `POST /specifications` creates a Draft with `parameters: []` (`api.ts:2521`).
- `PUT /specifications/:id` (`api.ts:2702-2729`) writes `req.body.parameters` straight in. There is no Zod schema for it and no per-item validation.
- `specificationSchema` (`lims.ts:47-51`) covers only material, version and effectiveDate.
- Specs do have a Draft to Active to Obsolete lifecycle with e-signature approval, optimistic version checks and audit entries (`api.ts:2731-2790`). That is spec versioning, not methods.

2. Spec parameters are copied into results, which acts as an implicit test plan.
- On sample registration (`api.ts:1578-1604`) every spec parameter becomes one `results` row with only name, min and max (`api.ts:1591-1600`).
- There is no per-sample or per-test selection, no test plan entity, no replicates and no method link. The bulk import does the same (`api.ts:~1675`).

3. A `unit` field exists only in the spec editor and types.
- `src/components/Specifications.tsx:239-243` and `src/types.ts:Specification.parameters` have a free-text unit.
- The seed specs (`seed_pg.ts:50-81`) have no unit.
- `results` has no unit column, and registration does not copy one.

4. OOS is a simple numeric range check, not a calculation.
- `api.ts:1834-1838` does `parseFloat(value)` and compares it to `specMin` and `specMax`.
- A non-numeric value such as "Complies" is never flagged OOS.

5. Mentions of RSD, SST and calculation are text only.
- `grep -i calculat src/server` hits only `api.ts:786, 852, 914, 999, 1016, 1037` and `seed_pg.ts:523`. These are AI prompt and fallback template strings for generated ELN worksheets and OOS CAPA text.
- `%RSD` hits (`api.ts:68, 79, 843, 911, 983-984`; `seed_pg.ts:513-514`; `ELN.tsx:671`) are the same kind of text: prompt strings, canned notebook content and seeded demo rows.

- `/reports/trends` (`api.ts:1425-1470`) only collects `parseFloat` values per batch. It computes no statistics.
- There are no tests for any of this in `tests/`.
- Branch `main` has nothing extra: `git grep` of `main` for stdev, rsd and calculat finds nothing beyond the same prompt text.

defects: CRITICAL - MFA bypass: the pre-MFA tempToken is accepted as a full session. login-local signs { id, temp:true } with the same JWT_SECRET (src/server/api.ts:2242). requireAuth only calls jwt.verify and loads the user by decoded.id (api.ts:1108-1119). `grep -n '\.temp' src/server/api.ts` shows the flag is read only at 2267 and 2303 (the TOTP routes). A user holding only the password gets a 5-minute Bearer token valid on every requireAuth route. The OQ-08 TOTP checks never call a protected route with a tempToken, so GX-10 'Fixed' is not true.

CRITICAL - TOTP secrets disclosed. GET /api/training returns db.query.users.findMany({columns:{passwordHash:false}}) to any authenticated user (api.ts:1054-1056), so totpSecret, failedAttempts, lockedAt and email go to every role. GET /api/admin/users (Admin and QA) strips only passwordHash (api.ts:2975), so totpSecret is leaked there too. Column is plaintext (src/db/schema.ts:17). The Training page fetches this payload for all roles (Training.tsx:13-17).

HIGH - MFA is inert end to end. The server answers { requiresTotp, tempToken } (api.ts:2243) but Login.tsx tests data.requireTotpSetup / data.requireTotp (Login.tsx:52,56). An MFA user falls through to onLogin(undefined token). generateSecret and QRCode are imported (api.ts:1-2) but never used. There is no enrollment or recovery endpoint, so MFA can only be switched on by editing the database (which is how OQ-08 does it).

HIGH - Failed e-signature bookkeeping is rolled back on OOS closure (the GX-04 defect class, fixed only for sample transitions). api.ts:2403-2411 updates failedAttempts and writes a SignatureFailed audit row inside db.transaction and then throws, so both are rolled back. The error always reports '2 attempt(s) remaining' because attempts = user.failedAttempts+1 from the stale req.user snapshot. Password guessing on OOS closure is unlimited and unaudited. Specification approval has the same pattern: the audit write at api.ts:2742 is followed by a throw at 2743, and no counter is kept.

HIGH - No attempt counting at all on other credential checks: batch release (api.ts:608-612), calibrate (2802), training certify (1068), notebook e-sign (1754-1760), admin settings and users re-auth (2937, 2991) and backup (adminWithPassword, 3061). Counters elsewhere are read-modify-write on the req.user snapshot (1926, 2223), so parallel guesses all read the same value and get one increment.

HIGH - Any authenticated user can crash the whole server. POST /api/samples/:id/notebook reads { content, password } and calls content.trim() and verifyPassword(password, ...) at api.ts:1741-1760 outside any try/catch, in an async handler under Express 4.22.2 (package.json:44). A non-string value (`{"content":"x","password":123}` or `{"content":5}`) makes scryptSync/trim throw, which becomes an unhandledRejection, and Node 22 exits. Reproduced in isolation with the repo's own express and Node 22.22.0 (process exit code 1). The same pattern exists at api.ts:1065-1068 (certify) and api.ts:3061 (adminWithPassword). No global error middleware (grep '(err, req' finds nothing), no process.on('unhandledRejection') anywhere, and desktop/main.cjs:60 only shows a dialog and does not restart the server.

HIGH - Rate limiting and brute-force protection are ineffective and also throttle legitimate use. server.ts:18 sets 'trust proxy' to 1 with no proxy in front, so a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For becomes req.ip (reproduced: 'X-Forwarded-For: 9.9.9.9' gives req.ip 9.9.9.9), and the limiter at server.ts:30-35 is bypassed by rotating the header. There is no auth-specific limiter. In the Electron deployment every user is 127.0.0.1, so one shared bucket of 200 requests per 15 minutes covers all users and all views. When it trips it returns plain text, which the UI's res.json() cannot parse.

HIGH - Lockout semantics are inconsistent and can brick accounts. login-local locks by setting active=false and lockedAt=now (api.ts:2226-2227), a permanent denial of service: anyone who knows a valid email can lock the only Admin with 3 bad logins, and there is no auto-expiry or CLI unlock. E-signature lockouts set lockedAt = now+15 min but leave active=true (api.ts:257, 1967, 2407), while login refuses any non-null lockedAt forever (api.ts:2217). The Admin 'Unlock' button (AdminPanel.tsx:99-110, 258) sends { active:true }, and the server resets counters only when !targetUser.active (api.ts:3003-3005). For an e-sig-locked user it reports success and changes nothing, so the user can never log in again.

HIGH - Segregation-of-duties and authorisation holes on master data. 23 of 33 authenticated POST/PUT handlers have no role check (computed from the route table; e.g. api.ts:2512, 2531, 2551, 2575, 2594, 2626, 2656, 2702, 2731, 2796). Specification parameters (limits) can be edited and approved by the same analyst, with no training guard and no author column to compare (api.ts:2702-2729, 2731-2789, schema.ts:108-115), so a user can widen limits and self-approve so that OOS never fires. PUT /api/oos/:id accepts a free-text status plus rootCause/conclusion from any role even after closure (api.ts:2594-2624). That bypasses the e-signed /oos/:id/close, and the release gate only checks status 'Open' (api.ts:619). POST /instruments/:id/calibrate lets any role push an arbitrary newDueDate and force status 'Active' with no schema and no signature row (api.ts:2796-2827). A non-date newDueDate such as 'x' makes `new Date(due) < new Date()` false at api.ts:1825, silently disabling the calibration block. instrumentSchema also accepts any non-empty string for calibrationDueDate (lims.ts:46-50).

HIGH - Training self-certification. POST /training/:userId/certify lets an Admin or QA certify their own account (target is not compared to the actor), accepts any moduleName (even undefined, which is a 500), and sets the global hasCompletedSoftwareTraining flag that gates all e-signatures (api.ts:1061-1096). init-db creates the first Admin with hasCompletedSoftwareTraining=false (init-db.ts:38), so self-certification is the only bootstrap path.

HIGH - Production start mode is insecure. package.json:9 `start` runs `node dist/server.cjs` without NODE_ENV=production, so server.ts:44 takes the Vite dev-middleware branch and api.ts:33 falls back to the public secret 'dev-only-insecure-jwt-secret'. HOST defaults to 0.0.0.0 (server.ts:20). With the seeded ids (seed_pg.ts:28, 'usr-admin') anyone on the LAN can mint an Admin token. Only the Electron shell sets NODE_ENV=production (main.cjs:60). GX-01 only tests the old literal secret.

HIGH - Unauthenticated source and sourcemap disclosure. express.static(distPath) (server.ts:53) serves the whole dist/ directory, which contains server.cjs (7.1 MB), server.cjs.map (12.4 MB, original sources embedded via --sourcemap, package.json:8), init-db.cjs and backup-cli.cjs. main.cjs:62 sets DIST_DIR to that same directory, so GET /server.cjs.map works without login.

HIGH - No effective session control. Non-MFA tokens are fixed at 8h and ignore sessionTimeoutMinutes (api.ts:2245-2249); MFA tokens use it only as an absolute expiry (2282-2286). There is no idle logoff anywhere. AdminPanel.tsx:323 advertises it, but `grep -rn 'idle\|inactiv' src` finds nothing implemented. HIGH - Password policy settings are cosmetic and there is no way to create or change a password. minPasswordLength/requireUppercase/Numbers/Symbols are stored (api.ts:2918, 2941-2947) and edited in AdminPanel but never read. passwordExpiryDays only feeds requiresPasswordChange (api.ts:2288-2291, 2322-2325), which no UI reads. generatePasswordHash is imported (api.ts:2197) but unused. MEDIUM - Admin settings and user updates are unvalidated and not .strict(). PUT /admin/settings stores whatever it receives (api.ts:2933-2955). sessionTimeoutMinutes=0 or NaN makes jwt.sign throw for every MFA login, and maxFailedLogins=0 locks accounts on the first failure. PUT /admin/users/:id accepts any role string (api.ts:2987-3000) and lets an Admin demote or deactivate themselves or the last Admin.

MEDIUM - Duplicate route /api/audit/verify. The first registration (api.ts:1979-2025) has no role check and shadows the role-checked one (api.ts:2028-2071), which is dead code. /signatures/verify/:id (2096-2192) and /traceability/batch/:batch/verify-chain (715-761) also load the entire audit table per request for any authenticated user, a memory/CPU amplification.

MEDIUM - Socket.IO has no authentication. server.ts:15 constructs the server with only cors:{origin:false}, and there is no io.use / io.on('connection') anywhere (grep). api.ts:1850 io.emit('notification') broadcasts OOS details (sample id, parameter) to every connected socket, including any non-browser client on the LAN when HOST=0.0.0.0. MEDIUM - TOTP verification has no replay protection and no per-account throttle. The same code is accepted repeatedly within its window, the tempToken is reusable for 5 minutes, and the only brake is the spoofable IP limiter (api.ts:2263-2331).

defects: src/server/api.ts:1303-1304 reads `r.expirationDate`, but the column is `expiryDate` (src/db/schema.ts:128): `reagentsActive` and `reagentsExpired` on /api/dashboard are always 0. Not caught because tsconfig has no strict, so drizzle findMany() rows type as `{[x:string]:unknown}` (probe verified).

src/server/api.ts:1521 reads `r.isOOS`, but the column is `isOos` (wrong name originates in src/types.ts:30): /api/reports/metrics always reports 0 OOS failures, so the Pass/OOS chart is always 100 % pass.

src/server/api.ts:1979 and 2028 both register POST /audit/verify. Express runs the first (no role check, so any authenticated user can trigger a full-chain scan); the role-checked copy at 2028 is dead code. Injected by patch-api-audit.cjs, patch-api-verify.cjs and patch-admin-integrity.cjs.

src/server/api.ts:2408-2411 (OOS closure) and 2742-2743 (specification approval) write the failed-signature counter/lockout and SignatureFailed audit row inside the transaction and then throw, so they are rolled back: no lockout, no audit of failed e-signatures. Same shape as GX-04, which was fixed only for sample transitions (1964-1969). Calibrate (2796+), batch release (590+), sample notebook (1757-1760) and ELN sign (231+) never count or audit failures.

No UPDATE in src/server/api.ts includes `version` in its WHERE (27 `.update().set()` calls; grep empty) and no `FOR UPDATE` exists anywhere: lost-update window on result entry (1805-1843), contrary to AGENTS.md section 2.

src/server/api.ts:1568 and 1660: sample id = `(select * from samples).length + 1`. O(n) per registration and racy: the SELECT runs before the advisory lock inside writeAudit (src/db/utils.ts:45), so concurrent registrations produce the same id and one fails with a PK violation reported as 500.

src/server/api.ts:2594-2623 PUT /oos/:id accepts `status`, `assignedTo`, `rootCause`, `conclusion` straight from req.body with no Zod schema: a user can set status 'Approved' and bypass the e-signed closure flow at 2369. Violates the AGENTS.md section 3 .strict() rule.

Express 4 async handlers without try/catch (api.ts:1053-1058, 1545-1550, 1704, 2073-2092, 2689-2698, 2791-2794, 2829-2836): a DB error becomes an unhandled rejection; server.ts has no process.on('unhandledRejection') and no error middleware, so Node terminates the server (desktop/main.cjs:64 dialog).
src/server/api.ts:1848-1857: io.emit('notification') fires inside the DB transaction before the audit insert and commit; Socket.io has no auth (server.ts:15, no io.use).

src/server/api.ts:1306-1313: dashboard trendData is a hard-coded Jan-Apr series plus a derived May/Jun, presented as real data. api.ts:2880-2892: the activity heatmap injects Math.random() workload when fewer than 50 audit rows exist. api.ts:78-80: dictation returns canned text when no model key is configured. src/server/pdfWorker.ts:34 stamps 'Status: Official (System Generated)' on a CoA for a sample in any state. All conflict with ALCOA 'accurate/original'.

Timestamps: schema `timestamp` (without zone) + `defaultNow()` evaluated in the PostgreSQL session zone, but drizzle reads naive values as UTC (node_modules/drizzle-orm/pg-core/columns/timestamp.js:31): on a non-UTC PC sample created_at, audit_trail.timestamp and signatures.timestamp (inserted without a value at api.ts ~1943) are skewed by the UTC offset while app-supplied values are correct; the UI prints them (AuditTrail.tsx:82, SampleDetail.tsx:599 and 706). Separately backup.ts reads with the default pg parser and restore shifts every timestamp (see PLT-01).
src/server/backup.ts createBackup: loads all tables into memory and JSON.stringify's them twice; fails with RangeError at 536,870,888 chars (reproduced).

src/server/api.ts:2248 password login issues an 8 h JWT regardless of systemSettings.sessionTimeoutMinutes (used only on the TOTP paths 2285/2319); minPasswordLength/requireUppercase/requireNumbers/requireSymbols are stored (2933-2948) but never enforced and there is no change-password route.

src/server/rabbitmq.ts:27 `channel.nack(msg)` requeues by default (poison loop); :38 setInterval has no re-entrancy guard; :43 job ids from Math.random; jobs left 'processing' by a crash are never reclaimed; src/server/reports.ts:20-34 returns any user's job result to any authenticated user.

tsconfig.json: no `strict`, no `include`: `npm run lint` type-parses 143 root scripts plus dist/ and release/ (51 s) and gives false assurance for server code.

desktop/main.cjs:59-60 forks the server with silent:true and nothing reads its stdout/stderr, so server logs are lost; index.html:7-9 depends on fonts.googleapis.com (not offline-safe); src/db/index.ts has no `port` option and no statement_timeout.
strengths: DB-level immutability for audit_trail and signatures: BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE triggers re-applied on every start and again after restore (src/db/protections.ts:11-39, src/server/backup.ts restoreBackup). Keep this idempotent-at-startup pattern and extend it to any new append-only table.

writeAudit runs inside the caller's transaction and serialises the hash chain with pg_advisory_xact_lock(7001) (src/db/utils.ts:45). The pattern is sound; the work is to make it unavoidable (PLT-03), not to replace it.

Backup design is good in principle: REPEATABLE READ snapshot, AES-256-GCM with scrypt key, manifest with row counts and audit head, verify-after-write, restore only into an empty database, covered by OQ-09 (src/server/backup.ts, tests/backup-restore.sh). PLT-01 hardens it rather than rewriting it.

Electron shell is already hardened: loopback-only server on a random port, DPAPI safeStorage for DB password and JWT secret, sandbox plus contextIsolation, navigation lock, single-instance lock (desktop/main.cjs:1-12, 55-70, 107-110). Keep all of it.

Sample state machine is data-driven with segregation of duties (src/server/workflow/transitions.ts), and the sample-transition path commits failed-signature bookkeeping outside the rolled-back transaction (src/server/api.ts:1964-1969). This is the model the other signing endpoints should copy.
Zod .strict() input schemas exist for the core entities (src/lib/validations/lims.ts), and the OQ suite already proves they reject server-controlled fields.

desktop/schema.sql currently equals `drizzle-kit export` of src/db/schema.ts exactly (verified in this review by a sorted line diff: empty), so a clean 0000 baseline migration can be cut today with no reconciliation.
